target_customer: Defense, aerospace, radar, communications and research organizations needing high performance software defined radios
problem: Wireless system builders need wideband multi-channel radios that cut integration effort and cost compared with assembling many components.
business_model: Hardware product sales (SDR transceivers) plus custom engineering and integration

founders.name: Victor Wollesen
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; backgrounds not given.

founders.name: Brandon Malatest
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; backgrounds not given.

technical_complexity.rationale: Wideband multi-channel RF and FPGA design for small teams is hard and hardware heavy, with long design cycles.

defensibility.rationale: Proprietary RF and digital design and defense customer qualification are slow to replicate, though established SDR vendors existed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; the company still sells products as of 2024 per product news.

market_need_then: No dated demand evidence was found for 2012. Later releases target radar, electronic warfare and communications customers.

identity.visual_style: Engineering catalog style; products named Crimson, Cyan, Chestnut and Calamine

branding.brand_signature: Product family with color and mineral names (Crimson TNG, Cyan, Chestnut, Calamine)

brand_strength.rationale: Known in a narrow SDR and defense niche through trade press; no brand-level coverage found.

outcome_analysis: Per Vices is a Toronto SDR hardware maker founded in 2005 that joined YC Winter 2012 and is still shipping products, including a 40 GHz receiver announced in June 2024. Funding is unknown and no exit or distress was reported, so it appears to be a small, long-lived hardware business serving defense and research markets.
notes: Aggregators conflict: one reports 125K seed from YC in March 2012, CB Insights reports 20K total with later accelerator entries. Both unverified, so no round recorded. No competitor with a source dated near 2012 was found; the company's own competitive matrix names categories only. Founder backgrounds not found.
